# **Differential gene expression analysis using DESeq2**

| The differential gene expression analysis was performed using the DESeq2 R package.

| The three treated conditions: **Hg**, **CO2** and **Hg+CO2** were independently analysed against the control condition: **CT**, using the *Wald test* implemented in DESeq2 (pairwise comparison).
The threshold used were : **pvalue < 0.05** & **|log2FoldChange| > 0.5**.

| Regarding the **Hg** & **CO2** conditions, only few genes were differentially expressed : **5** (fig.1) and **15** (fig.2), respectively. However, **315 DEGs** were found in the **Hg+CO2** condition, suggesting a synergistic interaction between both stressors when they occur concomitantly.  
|
<br>

```{r, Figure1, fig.cap="Figure 1: Heatmap representing the relative gene expression level of the 5 DEGs between MeHg and CT conditions.", echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE,  dpi=300, fig.width=7, fig.height=6, out.height="6in", out.width="7in"}
tar_read(Heat2)
```

<br>

```{r, Figure2, fig.cap="Figure 2: Heatmap representing the relative gene expression level of the 15 DEGs between  *p*CO~2and CT conditions.", echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
tar_read(Heat3)
```

<br>

| As shown in the Figure 3 below, only one DEG was found to be common to all conditions but a substantial proportion of DEGs from **Hg** and **CO2** conditions were also affected by the **Hg+CO2** treatment (60% and 27%, respectively).


```{r, Figure3, fig.capt="Figure 3: Venn Diagram displaying the number of shared DEGs resulting from the three pairwise comparison.", echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=4, fig.height=3.3}
grid.newpage()
venn_object <- tar_read(VennDiagram)
grid.draw(venn_object)
```


| Only one DEG between Hg and CT conditions was annotated: *PUS7* (BP: rna metabolic process), who's found to be implicated in "intellectual" developmental disorder with abnormal behaviour (in human).

| In *p*CO~2 vs CT, 5 among the 15 DEGs are annotated: TGM3 (BP: protein metabolic process, development process and cell differentiation), CCDC154 (à regarder), TMEM63C (pas décrit chez les mollusques), clec-78 and HDDC3...

--> There is nothing evident from these to comparisons.

| Among the 315 DEGs from the **Hg+CO2** condition, **61 were up-regulated** and **254 were down-regulated** (cf. heatmap).
|

```{r, Figure4, fig.cap="Figure 4: Heatmap representing the relative gene expression level of the 315 DEGs between *p*CO~2+MeHg and CT conditions.", echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
tar_read(Heat1)
```

<br>

| **The functional enrichment analysis** was performed on the whole gene expression dataset used for the differential analysis with the GOMWU utility using a MWU-based method (see <https://github.com/z0on/GO_MWU>).

Overall, 158 biological processes were found to be significantly enriched in the **Hg+CO2** condition. The more significants are represented in Figure 5.

<br>

```{r, Figure5, fig.cap="Figure 5: Main biological processes found to be enriched in *p*CO~2+MeHg condition following the MWU-based method.", echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=8}
tar_read(HgCO2_BP_Plot)
```

| Noteworthy, among the main repressed GOterms are biological processes related to the defense of the organism against external stress (i.e. $*immune response*, *defense response*, *response to wounding*, *inflammatory response*, *protein activation cascade* etc.). This suggests a decrease of their ability to cope with external stress. A possible link to the alteration of anti-predatory behaviour may be discussed. Moreover, genes implicated in the development of musclar tissues (i.e. *muscle development* and *muscle cell differentiation*), along with the development of neuronal network (i.e. *defasciculation of motor neuron axon*, *axonal defasciculation*) are also repressed, corroborating behavioral evidences for the neurotixicity of the two stressors.

<br>

| On the other side, there is a clear induction of RNA processing-related genes (*ribosome biogenesis*, *RNA splicing*, *mRNA processing*) as well as putative epigenetic regulation (*chromatin organization*, *obsolete histone H3-K4 methylation*, *obsolete covalent chromatin modification*) which may be characteristic of a response to environmental stress. Based on this, investigating epigenetic modifications would be quite relevant. (**See also the growing literature on the topic**).

<br>

| To go further, a weighted gene co-expression network (WGCNA) analysis was performed. Its aim is to identify clusters of genes (*modules*) defined by a significant correlation of their expression. Then the correlation between the so-called *modules* and some behavioural/environmental traits is tested to define *modules of interest* (those exhibiting a significant correlation with a given trait). In these modules, we can (i) conduct a GO enrichment analysis and (ii) identify *hub genes* (i.e. the 1% or 5% most highly connected genes among the module, expected to be the more representative).

<br>

| Here, the analysis resulted in **34 modules that were tested against behavioural parameters** investigated by Antoine during his PhD (Figure 6). **Three modules of interest were found to be correlated with the uniform score**: Maroon, Steelblue and plum3. They encompass 994, 247 and 47 genes, respectively. A simplified representation of the modules has been displayed on Cytoscape applying edge threshold from 0.1 to 0.21 depending on network density (Figure 7).

<br>

![Figure 6: Module-Trait correlation matrix.](Module-Traits-Correlation.png)

<br>

![Figure 7: Modules positively correlated to the uniform score. Gene in green are hub genes. A) Maroon, B) Steelblue, C) Plum3.](UniformModulesCyto.jpg)

<br>

| In the Maroon module, 265 GO terms were found to be enriched, among which the more representative were mostly related to cell cycle/meiosis/mitosis (e.g. *DNA replication initiation*, *regulation of cell cycle checkpoint*, *chromosome movement towards spindle pole*, *centromere complex assembly*) along with some metabolic processes (e.g. *deoxyribonucleotide*, *tatrahydrofolate*) or the *epigenetic negative regulation of gene expression* (Figure 8).

<br>

```{r, Figure8, fig.cap="Figure 8: Main biological processes found to be enriched in the Maroon module.", echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=8}
tar_read(Maroon_BP_Plot)
```

| The Steelblue module was associated with 157 enriched GOterms. The more representative corresponds to repair of tissue injuries (e.g. *defense response*, *wound healing*, *positive regulation of epithelial cell proliferation*, *lymphocyte migration*) (Figure 9).

<br>

```{r, Figure9, fig.cap="Figure 9: Main biological processes found to be enriched in the Steelblue module.", echo=FALSE, warning=FALSE, message=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=8}
tar_read(Steelblue_BP_Plot)
```
